capitals.name: Bacatá (Funza, Bogotá savanna)
capitals.note: The page names four confederations (Bogotá, Tunja, Duitama, Sogamoso) and says Bogotá was 'the most powerful chiefdom at the conquest'; it names no capital of the whole. Coordinates are the gazetteer's for Bogotá. Hunza (Tunja) 5.5504N 73.37W and Suamox (Sogamoso) were the other seats.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 800-1539: the page gives about 22,000 km2 ('most of Boyacá and Cundinamarca, and minor parts of Santander'); the conquest page 25,000 km2. Three discs round Bogotá, Tunja and Sogamoso (19,500 km2, ratio 0.8-0.9 against the pages) stand for it. The page gives no date for the formation of the confederations; the infobox period is c. 800-1540.

ledger.note: c. 800: the Muisca of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense (infobox 'c. 800-1540'; Early Muisca 800-1200, Late Muisca 1200-1537 in the page's period table). The page gives no date for when the confederations formed and the dates conflict (current consensus puts the Herrera period at 400 BCE-1000 CE).

region.text: Bacatá, the zipa's confederation round Funza and the Bogotá savanna

ledger.note: 20 April 1537: Jiménez de Quesada beats the zipa Tisquesusa at Funza. 'Funza: conquered and founded on April 20, 1537'; Tisquesusa died of wounds after a night attack near Facatativá; first contact was in February 1537 and the expedition had left Santa Marta on 6 April 1536.

region.text: Hunza, the zaque's confederation round Tunja

ledger.note: 20 August 1537: Hunza falls. The zaque Quemuenchatocha is captured on 20 August 1537 (later released; he fled to Ramiriquí and died shortly after). Tunja is founded on 6 August 1539 by Gonzalo Suárez Rendón.

Late August or early September 1537: the Spanish reach Sogamoso. They reached the Iraca Valley on 25 August 1537 (early September in other sources); the Sun Temple was accidentally burned in early September.

region.text: Bacatá, the zipa's confederation round Funza and the Bogotá savanna

ledger.note: 6 August 1538: the Spanish found Bogotá. The page notes some historians propose 27 April 1539. The zipa Sagipa, who had made terms, died under torture in the Spanish camp at Bosa in early 1539.

region.text: Bacatá, the zipa's confederation round Funza and the Bogotá savanna

ledger.note: 1538: Bacatá, the Bogotá savanna, passes to the Spanish with the founding of Bogotá on 6 August 1538 ('Bogotá founded August 6, 1538').

region.text: Hunza, the zaque's confederation round Tunja

ledger.note: 6 August 1539: the Spanish found Tunja. Founded by Gonzalo Suárez Rendón; the last zaque, Aquiminzaque, was executed in early 1540.

region.text: Hunza, the zaque's confederation round Tunja

ledger.note: 1539: Hunza, the Tunja country, passes to the Spanish with the founding of Tunja on 6 August 1539.
15 December 1539: Tundama is defeated. Baltasar Maldonado defeats Tundama at the Vargas Swamp island; the last Muisca confederation is conquered.
December 1539: Sogamoso and Duitama (Tundama) pass to the Spanish.

ledger.note: December 1539: the Muisca Confederation ends. Infobox 'c. 800-1540'; conquest 1537-1540 ('Spanish victory'); the last public Muisca religious ceremony was held at Ubaque on 27 December 1563. The Muisca land passes to the Spanish Empire.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Muisca

zones.text: Bacatá, the zipa's confederation round Funza and the Bogotá savanna
Hunza, the zaque's confederation round Tunja

wars.outcome: Spanish victory under Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada: Funza (20 Apr 1537), Hunza (20 Aug 1537), Sogamoso (Aug/Sep 1537), Bogotá founded 6 Aug 1538, Tunja founded 6 Aug 1539, Tundama defeated 15 Dec 1539; the last zaque executed early 1540.
wars.note: More than 80% of the soldiers and horses died during the expedition. Muisca population fell 65-85% between 1537 and 1636.

wars.name: Muisca-Panche wars and the Battle of Tocarema
wars.outcome: Frequent warfare; the Muisca were beaten at the Battle of Tocarema (undated on the Confederation page); the conquest page dates Tocarema 20 August 1538 with the Spanish and Sagipa defeating the Panche.
wars.note: No border moved; Venegas Carrillo conquered the Panche 1543-44.

certainty.note: Power rested 'on recognition of authorities, sometimes several at once, rather than strict subordination'.
The conquest is dated by town (Funza, Hunza, Sogamoso, Bogotá, Tunja, Duitama); the zone limits are discs.

sources.title: Spanish conquest of the Muisca
sources.note: Expedition from 6 April 1536; Funza 20 April 1537; Hunza 20 Aug 1537; Sogamoso Aug/Sept 1537; Bogotá 6 Aug 1538; Tunja 6 Aug 1539; Tundama 15 Dec 1539; area 25,000 km2; zaque executed early 1540.

notes: Wikipedia's article is 'Muisca Confederation'; a confederation of chiefdoms, typed 'state' because the article and Cliopatria-style listings treat it as a polity. Cliopatria has no Muisca row. The infobox (c. 800-1540) and the conquest end (zaque executed early 1540) are one year after the Tundama defeat of 15 December 1539, the last land: end set to December 1539. The zipa and zaque reign lists are Piedrahíta's and the page calls them unreliable; there is no ruler strip. Rodríguez Freyle dates Bogotá's expansion to one year before the conquest, Piedrahíta spreads it over 67 years: no pre-1537 territorial events written. Guane (Martín Galeano, 1539-1551), Muzo (Luis Lanchero, 1539-1559) and Panche (Venegas Carrillo, 1543-44) are neighbours, not parts. The Spanish dossier (group am-06) should carry the mirror gains; Cliopatria's Spanish Empire shape reaches Colombia but is not checked here. The conquest page area (25,000 km2) differs from the Confederation page (22,000 km2).
